reading: GRÜN · §84 — A-G48's L2 and A-G51's L1 as navigated STATES of the served fixture, with A-G206's span declaration
scope: rendered-page interaction and computed style on a loopback build. No raster, no luminance, no sealed datum, NO NEW FIXTURE DATA.
motion: reducedMotion:reduce — these are structural states, not breath readings

A_G206_spanDeclaration.one_whatThisSpans: Four focus states of ONE served fixture (UTiHc2G2tn-Nh1fyJ6vFH): L0 resting, L0 with a body marked by focus, L1 with a pool open, L2 with a FIELD body open. Within each, every drawn body's rank, shelf, in-pool, lit, named, marked and computed opacity, plus the two targets A-G51 was given.
A_G206_spanDeclaration.two_whatThisDoesNotSpan: It spans ONE POPULATION — the five bodies of the shared ranking, 2 field and 3 shelf. It is NOT LV01-LV12: the twelve layout inputs exist as existing test data in test/support/mapping/vectors.ts (so B-7 permits them), but the façade serves one job-ranking payload and reaching the other eleven populations needs the façade to serve a chosen vector, which is a façade change and is NOT in this reading. It also does not span L3, a requirement open, or any raster quantity.
A_G206_spanDeclaration.three_whatWouldWidenIt: A façade route that serves `layoutInputs()[name]` as the job-ranking for a requested vector name. That is a transformation of existing test data rather than new data, so B-7 permits it; it is the next step and it is not pretended to be done here.

openObservation_coordinateClick.what: page.click() on the pool chip, with a body marked, reported success and left data-level at L0; el.click() on the same selector reached L1. Reproduced in isolation.
openObservation_coordinateClick.whatIsNotKnown: whether a REAL pointer is obstructed. Playwright's hit-testing refuses a click whose target is not the topmost element at the point, and it is stricter than a browser; it may also have clicked a stale position. This probe does not resolve it and does not claim a product defect.
openObservation_coordinateClick.howToSettle: read `document.elementFromPoint` at the chip's centre while a body is marked, and compare with the chip itself — a one-line check on a rendered page, and the right shape because it asks what is ON TOP rather than what a click does.
openObservation_coordinateClick.whyItIsRecorded: a click that succeeds and changes nothing is the same family as Turbopack exiting 0 with no build and `next start` reporting 200 on a LAN-exposed port — three today. The generalisable part is that a tool's success code describes the tool, not the artifact.

finding: All 4 states reached and confirmed from the product's own disclosure (data-level / data-pool / data-role / data-marked) before anything was measured in them. A-G48's L2 with a field body and A-G51's L1 are therefore STATES, not data — which is why B-7 was never actually in conflict with them, and the span declaration says exactly what is still owed: LV01-LV12 needs a façade route serving layoutInputs(), a transformation of existing test data rather than an invention.
